name: ACC1d-1-a-token-can-be-replayed
note: F8, settled by Mac: a token is spent once. Without this, a token captured off one hello is a name anybody can wear in that room for its whole lifetime.

name: ACC1d-2-the-vouched-name-comes-off-the-FRAME
old: return { name: r.claims.n, kind: r.claims.k, subject: r.claims.s };
new: return { name: m.name, kind: r.claims.k, subject: r.claims.s };
note: THE WHOLE SEAM. The name must come OUT of the token - a signed claim set beats a typed one, and after ACC1g there is no typed one at all. Read off the frame, the signature verifies and then names whoever the sender asked to be.

name: ACC1d-3-a-failed-token-is-a-quiet-downgrade
new: if (!r.ok) return { name: m.name, verified: false };
note: A client that MEANT to send a token and sent a bad one must hear so. Admitting it unverified is how a forged token and an expired one become indistinguishable from a client that sent none.

name: ACC1g-4-a-keyless-relay-admits-everybody
old: if (!this._verifyKey) return { error: 'sign-ins cannot be checked right now' };
new: if (!this._verifyKey) return { name: m.name, kind: 'guest', subject: 'acct-unchecked' };
note: THIS ARM CHANGED DIRECTION WITH ACC1g. While a token was optional, admitting an unnamed hello over a mistyped key was the lesser failure; with the wall at the door it IS the hole - a relay that cannot verify cannot tell an issued name from a typed one, so admitting everybody reopens exactly what the gate closes. What keeps a bad key from taking the game dark is the DEPLOY checking it against what the account service publishes.

name: ACC1d-5-config-may-LOOSEN-the-modules-ceiling
note: F8's second half (bible ACC1d D3). A generous number typed in wrangler.toml would silently grant long-lived tokens; MAX_TTL_S is the hard ceiling and config may only tighten it.

name: ACC1d-6-the-wire-admits-any-string-as-a-token
note: The shape check is the only bound before an unbounded string reaches WebCrypto on the relay. A megabyte of rubbish would be parsed, hashed and refused far more expensively than here.

name: ACC1d-7-an-absent-token-is-sent-as-null
note: `tok: null` is a MALFORMED token, not an absent one, and wire.js refuses it - so every signed-out player, and every player the account service could not answer, would be refused the connection entirely.

name: ACC1d-8-the-token-is-minted-once-and-reused
note: The relay spends a token once (D4). A held-over token is refused on the second connection, so the player's own reconnect - or their second room - would be the replay the relay is guarding against.

name: ACC1d-9-the-mint-is-unbounded
note: An account service that never answers would hold the hello for ever: a second Worker's bad minute taking the game offline, which is the exact coupling ACC0's two-Worker split exists to prevent.

name: ACC1d-10-a-late-token-is-sent-down-a-dead-socket
note: The mint is an await, and a room change or a drop during it replaces the socket. Without the re-check, the hello goes out on a closed socket and the token is spent on nothing.

name: ACC1d-11-a-bad-minute-signs-the-player-out
note: `rate`, `no-signing-key` and `offline` say NOTHING about whether the credential is good. Forgetting the session over one would make an account service outage a permanent sign-out on every device that tried to connect.

name: ACC1d-12-a-signed-out-player-asks-anyway
note: A round trip per socket on behalf of nobody, and a throw on the connect path where a null was the whole contract.

name: ACC1d-13-the-presence-session-sends-no-token
note: The seam built, verified and deployed, and nothing calling it. The relay would vouch for nobody and the whole slice would read as working.

name: ACC1d-14-the-chat-link-sends-no-token
note: The hub is where a name is READ. An unsigned name in chat is exactly the impersonation this arc exists to make visible.

name: ACC1d-15-the-relay-deploys-with-an-unchecked-key
old:
if [ "$want" != "$got" ]; then
            echo "::error::the relay's IDENTITY_PUBLIC_KEY is not the one the account service publishes - every identity token would be refused"
            exit 1
          fi
note: bible ACC1d D2: the key is a second copy of a fact the service publishes, and a stale one fails in the worst possible way - every hello refused as a bad signature with nothing saying why. The deploy is where that is free to catch.

name: ACC1d-16-an-account-outage-blocks-the-relays-deploy
old:
echo "::warning::/v1/pubkey did not answer - the relay's key could not be checked against it"
            exit 0
new:
echo "::error::/v1/pubkey did not answer - the relay's key could not be checked against it"
            exit 1
note: A service that does not answer is not a mismatch. Refusing the relay's deploy over a SECOND Worker being slow is the exact coupling D1 and D2 both refused.

name: ACC1d-17-a-freshly-minted-pair-strands-the-relay
note: The deploy that can MINT a new pair is the one whose green run would leave the relay's configured copy wrong. Checking anywhere else is checking after the damage.
